newsitem.title: THAILAND: Body armor big seller in run-up to Thai election.
newsitem.headline: Body armor big seller in run-up to Thai election.

text.p: Bullet-proof vests have been selling like hotcakes as canvassers for politicians running in Thailand's November 17 election rush to order body armour, a shop owner said on Thursday.
Orders for bullet-proof vests have jumped tenfold since the campaign got under way three weeks ago, the manager of a jungle trek equipment shop told Reuters.
He said he used to sell one or two body armour jackets a day, but since the campaign began he has been receiving orders for up 10 jackets daily.
"Most of our customers are politicians' cavassers," he said.
His supply of bullet-proof vests, which cost 25,000-40,000 baht ($1,000-1,600) each, is running low and he has placed an urgent order for more from the United States.

Police in Chachoengsao province, about 80 km (50 miles) east of Bangkok, said on Thursday an unidentified gunmen had fired at the stage during a rally for Chart Pattana Party candidate Itthi Sirilathaykorn the previous night, killing one canvasserand wounding six others.
Canvassers are usually the prime targets of hired gunmen because they are better known and more influential locally than the politicians themselves.

Police have said they were monitoring some 750 known gumen to protect the 2,310 politicians vying for the 393 seats up for grabs in the poll. The gunmen appeared to be most active in the northern provinces where the election is most hotly contested.
